title: Confirm or Undo?
intro: Choose by frequency and severity. Frequent, low-impact actions get Undo; rare, severe ones get a confirmation — typed, if the stakes are high.

learn.title: The severity × frequency grid
learn.text:
**Frequent + low impact** → Undo by default.
**Rare + low impact** → one click, no interruption.
**Frequent + severe** → Undo, plus a warning.
**Rare + severe** → confirmation, typed if the stakes are high.

Most actions are reversible, so Undo is the default. Confirmation interrupts the flow — make sure it's worth it.

try.q: Users archive items dozens of times a day. Which guardrail fits?
options: A warning banner above the list
try.explain: Frequent and low impact: don't interrupt, let them reverse it.

left.label: Confirmation
items: Typed confirm for the worst cases

learn.title: Truly irreversible actions
learn.text:
Only a few actions genuinely can't be undone:

• Deleting linked items
• Removing data from other people's accounts
• Disconnecting devices
• Leaving without saving

**If you can't make it undoable, delay it** — for example, 15 minutes before a permanent delete actually runs.

try.q: A delete can't be reversed by the system. What's the fallback?
options: Delay the action so it can still be cancelled
Show two confirmation dialogs in sequence
Require an admin to approve it
Email the user a copy of the deleted data
try.explain: A delay turns an irreversible action into a reversible window.

learn.title: Label the outcome, not the dialog
learn.text:
Use **specific verbs**: Delete, Leave, Unsubscribe, Stay. Add “forever” or “permanently” when it is.

No **double negatives** — “Cancel cancellation?” is a trap.

For high-severity actions, ask the user to **type a name** to break the instinctive click.

And put Undo in a **persistent button**, not only a toast that fades away.

try.q: What is wrong with “Yes” and “Cancel” as dialog buttons?
options: They don't say what will happen
They are too short to tap accurately
They imply the action is reversible
try.explain: Label the outcome: Delete forever, Stay on this page.

test.q: What is the default guardrail, according to this note?
test.explain: Most actions are reversible, so Undo should be the norm.

test.q: When is a typed confirmation worth it?
options: Any action affecting more than one record

test.q: Why is a toast a poor place for Undo?
options: It blocks part of the interface
test.explain: Undo should be a persistent button.

options: Removing data from another person's account
Deleting a draft you just wrote
test.explain: Along with disconnecting devices and leaving without saving.
